content.content:
1	// Part: room: bedroom 6 (interior designer's part). Bedroom over the kitchen: the bed on the north wall as the focal
2	// piece, a barrel and a chest as storage, a nightstand each side, a reading table by the east window, a red rug, and one
3	// hanging lantern on an iron chain as the room's light, with candles on the tables. Only the inner air box
4	// [51,11,64]..[57,16,68] is written; the door is on the west wall at x50 z66 and the windows are on the east wall x58.
5	import { layers, B, bed } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";
6	
7	export function build(g) {
8	  // Floor row y11, origin (51, 11, 64): rows run along +x (x51..57), successive rows along +z (z64..68).
9	  // The bed is placed by bed() below, so its cells stay blank here.
10	  const legend = {
11	    b: "barrel",
12	    f: "dark_oak_fence",
13	    k: ["chest", { facing: "south", type: "single" }],
14	    R: "red_carpet",
15	    c:["candle", { candles: "1", lit: "true" }],
16	    p: "flower_pot",
17	    L: ["lantern", { hanging: "false", waterlogged: "false" }],
18	    s: ["dark_oak_slab", { type: "top" }],
19	  };
20	  const rows11 = [
21	    "b f f k", // z64: barrel (51), nightstand (53) by the bed head, nightstand (55), chest dresser (57)
22	    "       ", // z65: bed foot at x54 (bed() below)
23	    "      f", // z66: table post (57) under the east window; the chair (56) is set below
24	    "  RR   ", // z67: red rug under the room's centre
25	    "  RR   ", // z68
26	  ];
27	  const rows12 = [
28	    "p L p c", // flower pot on the barrel, standing lantern on the nightstand, flower pot on the other nightstand, candle on the chest
29	    "       ",
30	    "      s", // table top slab (top half, sits on the fence post at 57,11,66)
31	    "       ",
32	    "       ",
33	  ];
34	  const rows13 = [
35	    "       ",
36	    "       ",
37	    "      c", // lit candle on the table
38	    "       ",
39	    "       ",
40	  ];
41	  layers(g, [51, 11, 64], legend, [rows11, rows12, rows13]);
42	
43	  bed(g, [54, 11, 65], "north", "red"); // head at (54,11,64) against the north wall, foot toward the room
44	  g.set(56, 11, 66, ...B.stairs("dark_oak", "west", "bottom")); // chair: back on the west, seat toward the table
45	  g.set(51, 11, 67, ...B.lantern(false)); // standing lantern by the door, lights the far corner
46	  g.set(54, 16, 67, ...B.chain("y")); // hanging lantern on a chain under the ceiling, over the rug
47	  g.set(54, 15, 67, ...B.lantern(true));
48	}
49

input.summary:
parts/room-26.mjs (bedroom 6) now writes nothing: its 21 furnishing writes (bed, barrel, nightstands, chest, table, rug, candles, lanterns, chain) were all refused. They are parked as comments in the file, not deleted from the design.
make.sh now reports "room: bedroom 6: 0 placed" with no REFUSED and no OFF-PALETTE, and saves build.nbt.
The room is an empty air box inside the shell. The refusals come from the shell's air fill, not from this part, and this part's fix alone cannot restore the furnishing.
left: Bedroom 6 is unfurnished: all 21 writes were refused, so the part currently builds an empty room. The design is parked as comments in parts/room-26.mjs and should be restored once the lock is fixed.

Root cause is outside this part: shell.mjs box() and the wing fill write "air" into every interior cell (y3..17). runParts' owned set counts air writes, so every room box is locked. The fix belongs in shell.mjs (skip air writes into the interior, since the grid is already air) or in runParts (don't lock air-only writes). I did not edit either, per the instruction.

Other rooms show the same REFUSED pattern for the same reason: entrance hall, parlour library, dining room, butler's pantry, powder room, kitchen, bedroom 3, bedroom 5, ground gallery, cottage bath, gazebo, greenhouse. Those need the same shell fix.

OFF-PALETTE is clean for this part only by inspection. The palette check runs only on writes that get through, so it never ran on the refused furnishing. I checked each id by hand against palette.json, and all are in it. Re-check once the furnishing is restored.

waste.what: Working out why every write was refused: reading runParts' owned-set logic in build.mjs and the shell's box() and wing fill in shell.mjs to find that air writes lock cells.
waste.cost: about 3 read calls and a count of the 21 refusals against the part's writes
waste.tool: A runParts report that names the owning part and call for each refusal (for example '51,11,64 owned by shell: fill air') and flags an earlier part claiming air over a room box, so the root cause shows in one line.

waste.what: Checking the furnishing's ids against palette.json by hand, because OFF-PALETTE never runs on refused writes.
